title: Progression Models in Resistance Training for Healthy Adults
appliesTo: Dynamic resistance exercise repetition ranges, progression, rest and controlled execution
limitations: Family-level programming evidence; it does not validate every named variation independently

title: Resistance Training Guidelines infographic
appliesTo: Strength, hypertrophy and power loading ranges plus gradual progression
limitations: Summary infographic; record-level mechanics come from the movement-specific sources below

title: Flexibility Exercise (Stretching)
appliesTo: Comfortable, pain-free stretching performed slowly for 10 to 30 seconds
limitations: General flexibility guidance, not a rehabilitation prescription

title: Balance Exercise
appliesTo: Supported-to-unsupported balance progression and short single-leg holds
limitations: General-population guidance; people at fall risk should seek clinical advice

title: Plyometric Exercises
appliesTo: Low-volume, high-quality plyometric contacts with movement mastery before progression
limitations: Family-level guidance rather than a dose for a particular athlete

title: Increase Hip and Trunk Stability with Loaded Carries
appliesTo: Farmer, suitcase, rack, overhead and bottoms-up carries prescribed by time or distance
limitations: The article explicitly notes limited evidence for universal loading and volume rules

title: Weightlifting for Sports Performance
appliesTo: Staged teaching, technical quality and coached progression for clean and jerk derivatives
limitations: Sport-performance guidance, not a substitute for in-person coaching

title: CrossFit Gymnastics Course Seminar Guide
appliesTo: Prerequisite strength and progression for ring, pull-up, dip and body-control skills
limitations: A coaching manual rather than comparative clinical evidence

title: The Rope Climb (Wrapping)
appliesTo: Foot-clamp rope-climb progression and controlled ascent/descent
limitations: Technique reference; ceiling, anchor and landing safety still require local inspection

title: Men's Artistic Gymnastics Code of Points 2025–2028
appliesTo: Named planche, lever, L-sit and rings holds, including two-second competition recognition
limitations: Competition recognition is not a beginner training prescription

title: IWF Technical and Competition Rules & Regulations 2025
appliesTo: Clean-and-jerk receiving, lockout and completion standards
limitations: Competition rules define valid execution but do not prescribe novice training volume

title: Rules During Performance
appliesTo: Kettlebell clean, jerk, long-cycle, snatch, rack and fixation standards
limitations: Competition standards; general-population defaults remain conservative

title: ACE-Sponsored Research: Kettlebell Training Kicks Butt
appliesTo: Coached familiarisation with swings, snatches, cleans, presses, lunges and Turkish get-ups
limitations: Small study and not a technique authority for every kettlebell variation

title: The Two-Handed Kettlebell Swing
appliesTo: Ballistic hip-hinge mechanics and quality-stop cues
limitations: Technique article, not a universal loading prescription

title: Effects of Functional Steel Mace Training on Physical Fitness and Sport-Specific Performance in Elite Wrestlers
appliesTo: Steel mace 360, 10-to-2, offset press, offset squat, rotational lunge and single-arm swing
limitations: Elite supervised male wrestlers; the study's 20% body-mass load must not be generalized to novices

title: Steel Mace Benefits and Uses
appliesTo: Steel mace 360, uppercut, cross-body lunge, pressing and overhead walking mechanics
limitations: Manufacturer coaching content; used only for named mechanics, not efficacy claims

title: Rules & Regulations
appliesTo: Strongman carry, sandbag and atlas-stone event identity and completion standards
limitations: Event rules do not establish safe novice loads

title: The Safest and Riskiest Forms of Resistance Training
appliesTo: Gradual coached introduction of Olympic lifting, strongman and high-intensity power work
limitations: Risk-management guidance rather than exercise-specific efficacy evidence

title: Comparison of Resistance Training versus Static Stretching on Flexibility and Maximal Strength
publisher: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
appliesTo: Modified, light Jefferson curl executed with a three-second eccentric and one-second concentric
limitations: Healthy active adults and a modified exercise; no basis for heavy loading or symptomatic spines

title: Comparison of Controlled Articular Rotations and Static Stretching on Hip Internal Rotation Range of Motion
appliesTo: Slow hip controlled articular rotations through available range
limitations: Acute hip-ROM study in young adults; shoulder and ankle CAR entries use the same quality principle but are not claimed to share the outcome evidence

title: The Fitness Race
appliesTo: Official eight-station race order
limitations: Event order only
